Each company's latest full year, in $ million; how each figure is built: p. 25. Layer revenue: its companies added together; margins and returns: its median company. A layer is
ranked only on a median of at least 5 companies with the figure; a layer with fewer is shown, not ranked. A median is shown for 3 companies or more. Companies: those in the
layer's calculations, “of” those the layer lists where some are left out (who and why: the layer's page). A layer marked (adjacent): most of its companies' principal business is
another kind than the theme's core members'; shown, in no total, median or ranking of the theme. The theme's totals are of its 14 core members with figures. Layers whose
medians include whole-company (consolidated) figures of companies that also earn another way, no segment figures stored for them: Merchant acquiring and processing (2);
Payment platforms and crypto exchanges (1); Software products and subscriptions (1); each layer's page names them. These layers earn in 2 different ways: fees on the value or
number of payments they process; fees for trading, settling, holding or rating securities. Their figures are of different kinds of business, so they are set side by side and never
ranked against each other: a ranking is made only among layers of one way of earning.

Each of these layers has 2 member companies or fewer, so it has no median (a median is of 3 or more) and no page of its own; it is in the value chain's table. Rows in the value
chain's order; each company's latest full year; how each figure is built: p. 25. What each layer does (written by AI from general knowledge, with no figures): Card networks:
networks connect issuing and acquiring banks and authorise and settle transactions; Payment platforms and crypto exchanges: these companies run online payment systems
and digital asset trading platforms, with PayPal moving money online and Coinbase serving as a crypto exchange; Digital banks: app-based banks gather deposits and sell cards,
loans and investment products.
